In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the role that BDNF plays in the regeneration of a neuronal system in which the turnover of its cells is a continuous process.
the role of neurotrophic factors in the neuronal turnover process, with a view to developing an experimental model to study this process in vivo.
the role of neurotrophins in the regenerative capacity of the vertebrate olfactory tissue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the model developed in the present study is useful to study the role that BDNF plays in the regeneration of amphibian OE.
the amphibian larval olfactory system is an excellent model for studying the neurotrophic and neurogenic roles of BDNF and other neurotrophic factors in vivo.
the model developed in this study is suitable for studying the participation of Bdnf in the recovery of OE after damage in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of zinc sulphate as a toxic agent for amphibian larvae is a useful tool to study the role that neurotrophic factors have on the neuronal turnover of amphibian olfactory epithelum.
we developed a suitable model to investigate the role of brain derived neurotrophic factor in neuronal turnover of the amphibian olfactory epithelion.
we developed a suitable model to investigate the role of BDNF on the neuronal turnover in a vertebrate system.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the amphibian olfactory system is a good model to study the neuroregenerative potential of BDNF and other trophic factors, and that the experimental design described herein could be used to investigate other aspects of olfactory regeneration in amphibians.
amphibian larvae can be used as a suitable model to test hypotheses regarding the role of BDNF and other trophic factors in the neuronal turnover process of the olfactory system.
the amphibian larval system could serve as an experimental model to study the mechanisms involved in the regeneration and repair of the OE in vivo.
